title: Caribbean Sea Volume 1: Bermuda, Bahamas and the islands

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: A voluntary Vessel Traffic Management Service (VTMS) is in effect for vessels passing within 30 miles of Bermuda and is mandatory for vessels sailing for ports in Bermuda or intending to navigate within the Area to be Avoided. The following is a summary of regulations dealingwith vessel movements, berthing, and the duties of masters: 1.

calls.quote: Vessels passing within 30 miles of Bermuda are requested to contact Bermuda Harbour Radio on VHF channel 16 initially, stating: 1.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Oceanographic buoys have been reported about 13 miles S of Saint David’s Head.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Entry at night is dangerous and prohibited and a close approach at night should not be attempted without local knowledge. Three sub-surface moorings and one surface mooring have been established 50 miles SSE of Bermuda. Equipment is deployed for the purpose of scientific study on pollution and sediment.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all ports in Bermuda, except for yachts, and is available during daylight hours only. The pilot boards 3 miles E of Saint David’s Light for deep-draft vessels and 2 miles ENE of St. David’s Light, in the vicinity of SB lLghted Buoy, for all other vessels. The pilot boats have a black hull with orange or white superstructures and the words Pilots or Pilot Rescue on the side.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Inbound vessels must wait for outbound vessels which, whether approaching or in either Dundonald Channel or Two Rock Passage, have the right of way until well clear and, to indicate this right, hoist their national flag. 2. No vessel should enter Dundonald Channel or Two Rock Passage if it cannot do so safely. 3.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for non-exempt vessels at Freeport, Nassau, Douglas Road, Hanover Sound, Salt Cay Anchorage, and at South West Bay at New Providence Island; at Hatchet Bay at Eleuthera Island; and at Ragged Island where necessity allows entry without a pilot. Pilots for the anchorages in the vicinity of New Providence Island may be obtained off the bar at Nassau, but vessels proceeding to South West Bay may make arrangements to board the pilot at Goulding Cay.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels of 400gt or greater. Vessels using Freeport Harbor and Buckeye Hub should send their request for pilots at least 1 hour before arrival to confirm ETA. Vessels should send ETA 24 hours in advance. For pilot contact information see the table titled Freeport—Pilot Boarding Locations .

notes.quote: Freeport—Pilot Boarding Locations Buckeye Hub 26°28'75''N, 78°45'25''W Freeport 26°28'55''N, 78°47'75''W

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Due to shoaling, vessels should remain at least 4 miles offshore until permission to proceed is granted. Tankers waiting to berth normally remain about 5 miles off - shore. During daylight, vessels remain at least 4 miles offshore until SSW of the harbor entrance; vessels then proceed on the entrance range, or approach the oil berths on NNE course.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage for the terminal is compulsory to the sea island and the inner berths. Vessels should forward their ETA to the terminal upon on leaving the last port of call 72 hours, 36 hours, and 24 hours prior to arrival. Pilots board at position 26°34'45.0''N, 78°13'39.6''W. Vessels should also establish contact via VHF channel 16 when within radio range of the port.

notes.quote: Tugs and pilots can be contacted on VHF channel 73 and terminal oil operations on VHF channel 74.
The loading master will board about 2 miles S of the sea island, but may meet the vessel at another location specified by the pilot.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is available from Nassau pilots upon request. Pilots board 2 miles SW of the entrance. Vessels should call the port 2 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels calling at the Clifton Bluff area. Pilots board off Clifton Pier; not less than 24 hours advance notice is required.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: All vessels arriving from foreign ports should contact the harbormaster on VHF channel 16 for information and instructions before anchoring. Many traditional anchorage areas are now within the boundaries of six National Marine Parks. Vessels over 18.3m in length may not anchor within these boundaries.

items.head: Signals
items.quote: Vessels bound for any port in the Turks and Caicos islands must forward their ETA to the appropriate harbormaster on VHF channel 16. The message should include the vessel’s name, call sign, nationality, length, draft, and gross registered tonnage, and net registered tonnage.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory. Pilots can be contacted on VHF channel 16.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory but may be obtained from Grand Turk (Cockburn Town), Grand Turks Island.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: All vessels arriving from foreign ports should contact the harbormaster on VHF channel 16 for information and instructions before anchoring.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not available.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory. Pilots board about 1 mile off the reef.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A prohibited anchorage area and two subma- rine cable areas lie off the W coast of the island and may best be seen on the chart.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all foreign vessels. The vessel should send its ETA to Mambisas Habana. An ETA message addressed to Mambisas (name of port) should also be sent, if the vessel’s first port of call is not Habana. Pilots are available day and night and should be requested 72 hours in advance with an updated ETA being reported 24 hours in advance.

items.head: Signals
items.quote: Vessels must establish communications with the port signal station either on VHF channel 16, or visual signals to announce their presence, nationality, and characteristics.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: An area in which navigation has been prohibited has been established between an area bounded by the coastline to the SE and between a position 5 miles NW of Cayo Piedras del Norte Light (23°15'N., 81°07'W.), to a position 2.5 miles NNW of Punta Maya Light (23°06'N., 81°29'W.). A superbuoy lies in the Straits of Florida about 8 miles S of Woman Key.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Vessels not intending to use the Traffic Separation Scheme off Cabo San Antonio should avoid it by as wide a margin as is practicable. A description of the E coast of Mexico may be found in Pub. 148, Sailing Directions (Enroute) Caribbean Sea, Volume II. Cabo San Antonio to Mariel

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots are arranged through Mariel with advance notice and will board off Pasa Honda. The channel is navigated during daylight hours only.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and can be ordered from Mariel 48 hours in advance (see paragraph 4.12). The pilot embarks 1 mile N of the Pasa Honda. El Pan de Guajaibon (22°47'N., 83°22'W.) is one of these higher interior hills lying 13 miles SW of the town of Bahia Honda. It has a conspicuous 692m saddle-shaped summit, and is a landmark in identifying the bay from the open sea.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: For pilotage information, see Mariel (paragraph 4.12).

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: For pilotage information, see Mariel (paragraph 4.12).

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Navigation by civilian vessels is prohibited in Ensenada de Lazo and along the S side of the Peninsula Agosta. The vessel’s ETA should be sent on departure from last port, 10 days, 7 days, 5 days, 72 hours, and 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Caution— Navigation of civilian vessels is prohibited in Ensenada de Laza and along the S side of Peninsula Angosta on the west side of the harbor. Mariel to La Habana

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A restricted area, best seen on the chart, which is prohibited to all tankers, dry cargo vessels and vessels with a carrying capacity of more than 150 tons except tour ships, extends as much as 7.5 miles offshore between Punta de la Maya (23°06'N., 81°29'W.) and Cayo Piedras del Norte (21°58'N., 81°07'W.).

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory in Bahia de Cardenas and for its immediate seaward approaches. Pilots board off Matanzas; if bound for the facilities at Cardenas, they must arrive at least 3 hours before sunset so as to navigate the approximately 14 miles to destination during daylight only. From the pilot’s boarding point to the facilities, there is about 4 hours sailing time, including maneuvers to the Jose A. Echavarria Pier in Cardenas.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Vessels intending to enter Bahia de Cardenas by way of the generally-used passage between Cayo Mono and Cayo Piedras del Norte, approach from the NW clear of the Restricted Area, steering a course such that the higher appearing islet Cayo Chalupa, about 5.5 miles distant, bearing 173°, lies a little open to port.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. For pilotage information, see Matanzas (paragraph 4.17).

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: In Canal de los Barcos vessels entering must give way to vessels leaving the port.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board in position 23°02'N, 79°59'W. See Matanzas (paragraph 4.17) for more information.

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Regulations

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: The pilot station is located in Antilla. Pilotage is compulsory for the ports of Antilla, Felton, and Nicaro. Pilots board vessels approaching from the E in position 20°48.2'N, 75°32.2'W, and vessels approaching from the W in position 21°06.8'N, 75°57.7'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: For pilotage information, see Antilla (paragraph 4.40). Vessels are urged to contact the local authorities for current information on the berths before docking. The berth here is reported to be able to accept vessels up to 177m in length with a maximum draft of 7.3m. One vessel at a time can be handled.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: see Antilla (paragraph 4.40) for pilotage information.

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards 2 miles NNE of the entrance to Quebrado de Moa, in daylight hours only. For more pilotage information see Puerto Cay Moa (paragraph 4.46).

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all foreign vessels. The vessel should send it ETA to “Mombisas Habana.” An ETA message addressed to Mombisas (name of port) should also be sent if the vessels first port of call is not Havana.

items.head: Regulations

items.head: Signals

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for ships engaged in foreign trade, but is not required for ships of the U.S. Navy. Permission to enter the U.S. Naval Reservation boundaries and request for pilotage should be secured in advance of arrival. See the General Remarks topic in paragraph 5.1 for information on Cuban pilotage.

notes.quote: Pilots board in position 19°53'52.2''N, 75°10'52.2''W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Unidentified ships are reported to the Harbor Police for investigation. The Harbor Entrance Control Post operates from the signal station atop a building on McCalla Hill (19°55'N., 75°09'W.).

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchorage is prohibited within 0.2 mile of any cable areas. Anchorage is prohibited between Leeward Point and Windward Point. These areas can best be seen on the chart. For vessels intending to remain at anchor for any length of time it has been suggested to anchor with at least 2.5 shots of chain as violent squalls may arise at any time.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Vessels should request pilotage 12 hours prior to arrival. Pilots board in position 19°56'N, 75°52'22.2''W.

items.head: Signals
items.quote: Vessels must establish contact with the signal station prior to entering the channel.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. The pilot boards 2 miles SW of Cabo Cruz. Entry into Bahia de Pilon during the daylight hours affords the mariner a clearer look at the many sunken dangers that can be recognized by a change in water color. Entry at night proceeds only as far as the outer harbor anchorage.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. See the General Re- marks in paragraph 5.1. Pilots board off either Cabo Cruz or 2.5 miles SW of Cayo Blanco if using Canal de Cuatro Reales. They commonly proceed to the destination by day or night.

notes.quote: It is recommended that a pilot be arranged at least 24 hours before arrival during the day and at least 48 hours prior if arriving at night, otherwise, many hours may pass before the pilot boards.
The pilots may be contacted on VHF channels 13 and 16.
For the boarding ground off Cayo Blanco, the pilots (call sign: Castilda Practicos) may be contacted on VHF channels 13 and 16.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Berthing and unberthing is available 24 hours. During unfavorable conditions, berthing and unberthing of vessels over 180m in length takes place during daylight hours only.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilots board at the seaward entrance to Canal de Breton, Canal Tunas, and Canal de Jobabo. It is compulsory to take a pilot and vessels must proceed to their destination during daylight hours only. Vessels proceed directly to Tunas de Zaza and Casilda which are the sub-ports to the harbor administration for Bahia de Cienfuegos, but must call at Jucaro first before continuing on to Ensenada de Santa Maria, Ensenada Boca Grande, or Palo Alto.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board vessels 1 mile WSW of Los Colorados Light. Service is available 24 hours. It was reported that a whirlpool is formed at Pasacaballos turn, during the rising tide, making navigation very difficult.

notes.quote: If vessels must wait until the pilot comes out, they are advised to lie to in such manner as to compensate for a general W set in offshore currents.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: If there is an inbound vessel in the channel, the outbound vessel must wait for the inbound vessel to clear the channel.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: They transit Bahia de Cienfuegos entrance in mid-channel as far as Punta Pasacaballos, where the sharp turn NNE must be negotiated with care, particularly when currents set seaward and bear full on the starboard bow. Vessels are advised to have the anchor ready to let go and, if need be, to run a line to a warping post standing on Punta Pasacaballos in order to heave the bow up into the current.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Vessels should request pilotage 6 hours prior to arrival. Pilots board in the following positions: a. 22°01'18''N, 80°27'30''W. b. 22°02'42''N, 80°27'24''W.

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Caution

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 800 gt, all cruise ships, and all tankers. The pilot boards in position 19°45.9'N, 79°45.8'W or in position 19°40.2'N, 79°52.9'W, and remains on board during all berthing, unberthing, and lightering operations, together with two assistants and two riggers to handle the fenders.

notes.quote: The pilot vessel (call sign: Bonito) may be contacted on VHF channel 16.
Vessels use VHF channel 16 (call sign: CBPA) for radio frequency information.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage for all ports in Jamaica is provided from Kingston. Pilots should be ordered well in advance to allow for the necessary arrangements to be made.

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

Vessels are cautioned that buoys in Port Morant are not always reliable and that a heavy swell usually sets into the inlet. It is reported that Port Morant is no longer used for commercial shipping and the aids to navigation are not maintained.

items.head: Pilotage

Gordon Cay (South Container Terminal) For pilot contact information, see the table titled Kingston—Contact information .

Quarantine and customs procedures require unexempted vessels to proceed no farther into Kingston Harbour than the harbor entrance, where they anchor in position close W of Chevannes Lighted Beacon and there await inspection.

items.head: Pilotage

Wathey Pier, but optional for the Shell Oil Terminal and the Texaco Oil Terminal in Cole Bay, although it is recommended for the first visit. Pilots board in position 18°00'23''N, 63°04'09''W. items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Caution

The N limit of the prohibited area is marked by lighted buoys. Within Baie de Saint-Jean, entry is prohibited for all vessels within an area which serves as an extension of the airport runway and marked by alternating yellow and red buoys.

Pilotage is also available for Woodbridge Bay Terminal (15°18.5'N., 61°23.9'W.); Rockaway Anchorage, about 1 mile N of Woodbridge Bay; and Belfast Anchorage (15°21.7'N., 61°24.8'W.).

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A circular firing practice area, with a radius of 12 miles centered on position 14°35.2'N, 61°47.6'W, lies about 37 miles W of Martinique.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchorage is prohibited in an area at the end of Saint- Pierre Jetty. This area is marked by three buoys.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels carrying hydrocarbons or dangerous cargo and/or vessels with an loa greater than 50m bound for the port or anchorage. The pilotage area is defined as E of a line joining the church tower at Le Car - bet and Pointe La mare. Pilots board in position 14°44.5'N, 61°11.7'W.

notes.quote: Caution .—The pilot boarding position is within a sea plane landing area.
A platform, with dolphins nearby, situated on the sides of the pier, can accommodate vessels up to 15,000 gt, with a draft of 9.1m.
Pilots board either at Fort de France or 1 mile NW of the berth.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A restricted area, best seen on the chart, lies 5 miles NW of Fort de France. Fishing is prohibited. Mariners are advised to navigate with caution in the area and consult the local port authorities for the latest information. Fort de France (14°36'N., 61°05'W.)

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels greater than 50m loa and all vessels carrying hydrocarbons or dangerous materials proceeding to anchorage or the port. Vessels less than 100m may enter the port and anchor without a pilot if they anchor W of a line that joins Fort Saint Louis and Pointe du Bout. For vessels with a draft greater than 11m crossing the line joining Pointe des Negres to Cap Saloman, the pilot- age zone is defined as E of a line joining Cap Salomon and Fond Bourlet.

notes.quote: All vessels must submit their ETA to the harbormaster's office through their agent either 24 hours before arrival or upon departure from the previous port if the voyage is less than 24 hours.
Additionally, vessels must contact the harbormaster on VHF channel 12 prior to arrival to obtain authorization to enter the port.
Any changes to ETA must be requested at least 2 hours in advance.
The pilot boards in position 14°35.4'N, 61°06'W.
Vessels should report 6 hours before arrival, including loa, beam, arrival draft, and if the vessel is equipped with thrusters.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: It is reported (2011) that the dayboards of the forward and after range markers are red and black with a white and black metal frame.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A large prohibited anchorage area containing submarine cables lies across the E portion of Baie de Fort-de-France, and may best be seen on the chart. Fishing is prohibited in a restricted area best seen on chart.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A restricted area is best seen on chart. Fishing, anchoring, and diving are prohibited. Speed restrictions are in force. An exposed wreck lies just outside the S channel entrance to Baie des Cyclones.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels carrying hydrocarbons or dangerous cargo, irrespective of loa, and for all vessels over 50m in length. Vessels awaiting a pilot must not proceed N or E of the pilot boarding position (14°26.6'N., 60°55'W.). Pilots are provided from Fort-de-France and at least 6 hours notice is required.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. At least 2 hours notice of arrival is required by the pilot station at Fort-de-France for the provision of a pilot. Caution .—A restricted area 5 miles S from position 14°41'39.6''N, 60°51'06.0''W to position 14°36'57.4''N, 60°49'33.0''W. Fishing is prohibited.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels carrying hydrocarbons or dangerous cargo and/or with an loa 50m or greater bound for the port or anchorage. Pilotage is provided by Fort De France. For pilot boarding locations, see the table titled Havre du Robert—Pilot Boarding Locations .

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels must send their ETA 6 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: See Havre du Robert (paragraph 9.11) for pilotage information.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels greater than 50m loa and all vessel, regardless of size, carrying hydrocarbons or dangerous materials, proceeding to anchorage or the port. Pilots board vessels 0.7 mile NE of Ilet Saint Aubin.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: The pilot boards approximately 3.5 miles W of Port Castries, and can be contacted on VHF channels 9, 16, and 65.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 100 gross tons and is available from 0500-0900 and 1600-2000.

notes.quote: The pilot boards in position 13°42'13''N, 60°59'02''W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Application for a berth must be sent by the vessel or agent 72 hours prior to ETA. A notice of ETA should be sent 48 hours prior to arrival and should include the vessel’s draft, ETA, and bunker requirements. Vessels should not approach within 3.5 miles of the port until radio contact has been established.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchorage is prohibited in the coastal area between Anse Jambon (13°52'N., 61°05'W.) and Anse L’Ivrogene (13°48'N., 61°04'W.). Marigot Harbour, a small inlet entered through a narrow channel, lies 0.75 mile NNE of Pilori Point. Anchorage may be obtained by small craft, in depths of from 5.5 to 8.2m, clear of the charted submarine cable.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 100 gt. Pilots board in position 14°00'54''N, 61°04'08''W. Pilots can be contacted on VHF channel 9.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Ves- sels should contact the port office on VHF channel 9 at least 3 hours before arrival at the pilot boarding position to advise any change in ETA.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 100 gt. Pilotage is available 0800-1630 and 1630-0800 on request. The pilot boards in position 14°01'22''N, 61°00'49''W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for tankers more than 100 gt. Pilots board in position 12°27.4'N, 61°30.3'W. For pilotage information, see Saint George’s (paragraph 9.48).

items.head: Caution
items.quote: The following activities are prohibited within the MPAs: 1. Anchoring, except in cases of emergency. 2. Fishing. 3. Diving without the supervision of an authorized local dive operator.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels of over 150 gt. See Saint George’s (paragraph 9.48) for pilot and port information.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels of more than 200 gt. Pilotage should be requested 24 hours prior to arrival and 3 hours prior to departure. The pilot boards in position 12°03'36''N, 61°46'12''W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels except naval vessels and small sailing yachts and is available 24 hours. The pilot boards 0.5 mile W of the Fairway Lighted Buoy in the anchorage area.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Long Shoal is an anchoring prohibited area which has a 250m underwater pipe that extends from the SW corner. A shoal, with a least depth of 4.2m, extends W of the Bulk Handling Wharf. Submarine cables lie off Needham Point and run WNW.
